Container.Name: masqueradarr.aio
Container.DefaultTagDescription: Uses the latest technology stack and mongodb version

Branch.TagDescription: Uses a legacy technology stack for older systems that cannot run the latest version of mongodb

Container.Overview:
masqueradarr is a self-hosted IPTV aggregator. It pulls channel playlists (M3U) and guide data (EPG/XMLTV) from a range of online IPTV services, normalizes them into one catalog, and serves them back as a single, unified, standards-compliant playlist + guide — behind one trusted identity that your media apps and IPTV clients can talk to.
Two images are published. The default :latest tag uses the latest technology stack and mongodb version. The :mongo4.4-latest tag uses a legacy technology stack for older systems that cannot run the latest version of mongodb. Community Applications asks which one to install; if you add this template by URL instead, edit the Repository field to switch.
Rebel IPTV (optional, off by default): masqueradarr can run or attach Rebel IPTV, a closed-source IPTV source licensed for personal, non-commercial use only. It always runs as its own unmodified rebeliptv/iptv container — masqueradarr never bundles or patches it. Set REBEL_IPTV_ENABLED=true to turn it on. In managed mode (REBEL_IPTV_URL empty, DOCKER_SOCK_ACCESS=1) a sibling container named masq-rebel-iptv appears in the Unraid Docker tab without a template. That is expected: don't edit it there, manage it from masqueradarr Settings → Rebel IPTV. Docker socket access is host-root-equivalent and off by default.

Config.Name: MASQ_EDGE
Config.Description: Optional (default off). 1 inverts the topology so the Rust proxy owns the public port

Config.Name: REBEL_IPTV_UI_HOST_PORT
Config.Description: Rebel IPTV dashboard pop-up (admin-gated). Only used when REBEL_IPTV_ENABLED=true. The container always listens on 3080; if you change the host port here, set REBEL_IPTV_UI_PORT to the same value.

Config.Name: MONGO_ROOT_USER
Config.Description: Update MONGO_ROOT_USER to set a different username

Config.Name: MONGO_ROOT_PASS
Config.Description: Update MONGO_ROOT_PASS to set a different password

Config.Name: DOCKER_SOCKET
Config.Description: Docker socket. Opt-in: leave blank to keep it unmounted. Only mount together with DOCKER_SOCK_ACCESS=1 — host-root-equivalent. The app user joins the socket's group; a socket that is root:root and not group-writable is refused (logged at startup), in which case run a docker-socket-proxy and set MASQ_DOCKER_HOST instead of mounting this.

Config.Name: DOMAIN
Config.Description: Update DOMAIN to match your local system or public domain

Config.Name: DOCKER_SOCK_ACCESS
Config.Description: App-wide Docker Engine API access: 0 = off, 1 = on (host-root-equivalent). Needed for Rebel IPTV managed mode, updates, auto-update, restart and logs. Requires the Docker socket mount (advanced) or MASQ_DOCKER_HOST. If the startup log says the socket is root:root and not group-writable, use a docker-socket-proxy and MASQ_DOCKER_HOST.

Config.Name: REBEL_IPTV_ENABLED
Config.Description: Run/attach the optional Rebel IPTV companion (true/false).

Config.Name: REBEL_IPTV_URL
Config.Description: Set = adopt a Rebel you run yourself (e.g. http://rebel-iptv:8080 on a shared network). Empty = managed: masqueradarr creates masq-rebel-iptv + masq-rebel-net + masq-rebel-iptv-data itself (needs DOCKER_SOCK_ACCESS=1).

Config.Name: REBEL_IPTV_IMAGE
Config.Description: Rebel IPTV image. A non-latest tag pins it (updates become notices only).

Config.Name: REBEL_IPTV_UI_PORT
Config.Description: Host port of the pop-up — must match the host side of the 3080 port mapping above.

Config.Name: REBEL_IPTV_UI_PUBLIC_URL
Config.Description: Full origin when the pop-up sits behind TLS/reverse proxy, e.g. https://rebel.example.com.

Config.Name: REBEL_IPTV_PUBLISH_PORT
Config.Description: Managed only: also publish Rebel's :8080 (HDHomeRun emulation) on this host port.

Config.Name: DOCKER_SOCK_PATH
Config.Description: Socket path inside the container if non-standard (default /var/run/docker.sock).

Config.Name: MASQ_DOCKER_HOST
Config.Description: Use a docker-socket-proxy instead of the raw socket, e.g. tcp://docker-sock-proxy:2375. This is the workaround when the socket is root:root and not group-writable.

Config.Name: MASQ_SELF_CONTAINER
Config.Description: This container's name/ID, only if auto-detection fails (needed for managed mode to join masq-rebel-net).
